{{Short description|Twisted spin group}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Spin<sup>h</sup> group}}
{{One source|date=March 2025}}
In [[spin geometry]], a '''spin<sup>h</sup> group''' (or '''quaternionic spin group''') is a [[Lie group]] obtained by the [[spin group]] through twisting with the first [[symplectic group]]. H stands for the [[Quaternion|quaternions]], which are denoted <math>\mathbb{H}</math>. An important application of spin<sup>h</sup> groups is for [[Spinh structure|spin<sup>h</sup> structures]].

== Definition ==
The [[spin group]] <math>\operatorname{Spin}(n)</math> is a [[Double cover (topology)|double cover]] of the [[special orthogonal group]] <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math>, hence <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math> acts on it with <math>\operatorname{Spin}(n)/\Z_2\cong\operatorname{SO}(n)</math>. Furthermore, <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math> also acts on the first symplectic group <math>\operatorname{Sp}(1)</math> through the [[Antipodal point|antipodal]] identification <math>y\sim -y</math>. The ''spin<sup>h</sup> group'' is then:<ref>Bär 1999, page 16</ref>

: <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(n)
:=\left(
\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\operatorname{Sp}(1)
\right)/\mathbb{Z}_2
</math>

mit <math>(x,y)\sim(-x,-y)</math>. It is also denoted <math>\operatorname{Spin}^\mathbb{H}(n)</math>. Using the exceptional isomorphism <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(3)
\cong\operatorname{Sp}(1)
</math>, one also has <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(n)
=\operatorname{Spin}^3(n)
</math> with:

: <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^k(n)
:=\left(
\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\operatorname{Spin}(k)
\right)/\mathbb{Z}_2.
</math>

== Low-dimensional examples ==

* <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(1)
\cong\operatorname{Sp}(1)
\cong\operatorname{SU}(2)
</math>, induced by the isomorphism <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(1)
\cong\operatorname{O}(1)
\cong\mathbb{Z}_2
</math>
* <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(2)
\cong\operatorname{U}(2)
</math>, induced by the [[exceptional isomorphism]] <math>\operatorname{Spin}(2)
\cong\operatorname{U}(1)
\cong\operatorname{SO}(2)</math>- Since furthermore <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(3)
\cong\operatorname{Sp}(1)
\cong\operatorname{SU}(2)
</math>, one also has <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(2)
\cong\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(3)
</math>.

== Properties ==
For all higher abelian [[homotopy group]]s, one has:

: <math>
\pi_k\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(n)
\cong\pi_k\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\pi_k\operatorname{Sp}(1)
\cong\pi_k\operatorname{SO}(n)\times\pi_k(S^3)
</math>

for <math>
k\geq 2
</math>.
